label: context.reference
description: Create, dispatch and receive Home Tasks through granted file writes and exact artifact routes.
text:
Author Home Tasks through granted file tools and artifact movement. Read this artifact in full with artifact.read for authoring_examples and run_record_schema.document. Examples illustrate exact identities and schemas; resolve live paths, descriptor bytes, tool ids, EE and interface ids from attested metadata, bound artifacts and granted file.read/file.list. Do not copy example identities into a Home.

1. Inspect. Home receives artifact-home-delivery; standard Tasks receive artifact-run-authoring-coordinates. Their authoring object lists record paths, tool mappings and declared read/write/execute rules. Exact door overrides supply concrete paths; host_binding_not_supplied means no machine path was supplied. Coordinates grant no rights. Use a visible composition operation's current schema when it prepares the required file/send effects. For manual authoring, read the current run, worker policy, EE chain, worker/provider/door descriptors and sidecars, tools and run schema. Check existing Tasks before creating one. Use the model catalog and provider policy; keep authentication private. Source access and execution require explicit grants, never the provider cwd. Choose a permitted EE; create a narrower project EE only when needed and authorized. Ordinary Tasks need no new EE.

2. Author owners. Choose independent exact worker/provider/tool-door/client identities where isolation requires them. Reuse code through explicit owner imports and copy required descriptor life/config sidecars; a driver reference imports no configuration. A worker pin has interface_type=system, role=worker and a policy.json ceiling, with no executable driver or life. It uses RuntimeRelay; an inert role=system folder cannot substitute. The worker pin can receive the Task. An existing Home worker pin can receive its return when that is the intended boundary; a separate return boundary needs its own permitted pin and Home checkpoint. Never infer callbacks from run ids.

3. Set policy. Add new exact ids to each restrictive EE layer and relevant worker ceiling through authorized writes, preserving unrelated entries. Null EE allowance is unrestricted at that layer; [] permits nothing. Every EE layer must allow the worker pin. Tools require their interface, owning WEK and bound door to survive formation. Families and source_names do not grant admission. Task authority comes from its own ceiling and EE chain, not Home's grant. Home may author a more capable Task only within its existing record-write authority.

4. Bind context. At every relevant checkpoint, bind the full required role-artifact closure for the worker and every worker relay surviving formation, using {id,access:{read:true}}. Missing roles fail formation; they are not attached automatically. Source worker roles describe their owners, not a command for the recipient to become Home. Include the assignment, constraints, selected evidence and return contract. Context is not inherited from provider history, a repository, the initiating run, project labels or memory profiles.

5. Write files. Use the granted writer. New files use content and expected_before_hash:null. Existing edits use observed expected_before_hash or expected_before_content to protect concurrent work. Use the file tool's declared hash algorithm; RFC 6902 patches also require expected_after_hash. A writes batch stages and validates but is not a cross-file atomic transaction; inspect reported paths/hashes after an error. Write descriptors, policies and artifacts before exposing the receiving run frontier. Read back installed bytes and check dependencies. Writing run JSON does not deliver an assignment.

6. Compose the run. Read run_record_schema.document here; its source and validation_source explain provenance and constraints, not filesystem authority. Cross-record/registry checks belong to the candidate validator. Give the run and every checkpoint a nonempty trace and list projected ids in active_checkpoints. Every active checkpoint needs an inbound interface binding. Task input binds its receive pin and routes to its provider. Tool-call checkpoints bind the provider, require tool.call.allowed via tool_call_allowed with params.tools limited to that door's tools, and route to that door. Tool results return separately to the provider. Provider progression uses the distinct narrow writer and source/door/result checkpoints in its installed contract. Preserve interface_state and unrelated checkpoints; use a new id or epoch for a new generation. A writable Task needs a real client interface/binding; otherwise its projection is read-only. Client sidecars remain client-owned.

7. Dispatch. Home needs the Task receive pin in its permitted active bindings; the Task needs an active input checkpoint on the same pin. An exact-name provider-output checkpoint can expose an outbound binding for model-selected artifact.send without forwarding every provider/tool artifact. Keep the executing checkpoint and door active during the send, with the target in the fresh grant and required readable worker roles bound. Restrict admission to the assignment/return vocabulary. artifact.send targets System interfaces, not World-provider/chat/time RPCs. Send the assignment after verifying file writes. admitted/seq confirms emission; a reader can consume it later. Do not duplicate admitted work while waiting. Repair a definite refusal deliberately; inspect evidence before repeating an uncertain effect.

8. Return. Bind the return address in the Task's active surface and ceiling, with an independent Home checkpoint listening. The example sends task.summary for completed, blocked and failed outcomes with status, summary and evidence. artifact_exists with task.summary.received confirms readable receipt. To verify completion, require the actual result label/verifier/mark, for example coder.build.result -> build_success -> coder.build.ok when installed and granted. Inspect registry/verifier and registry/mark before using them; author/install a missing owner through permitted writes. A tool-call-format check cannot verify a build. Put completion requirements on the checkpoint awaiting the result, never Home's operator-input checkpoint. Tasks may share a Home return pin; use separate exact pins for distinct policy/receipt boundaries. Do not route by payload labels. Rearm receivers with a new checkpoint generation.

Use one return path per outcome: either the example's explicit send or the installed provider's explicit terminal-output binding. For terminal routing, bind its success and error vocabulary and preserve output selection. Return the result, source Task/run identity, artifact refs and required verification evidence. Home decides outward delivery. Under checked_input_intake, notification_action=followup invokes the receiving model on unwrapped outcomes; queue stores context only. New intake templates select followup; preserve existing concrete configuration. Use queue when no automatic interpretation is intended. provider.peer.message keeps its declared meaning. Change intake consistently in its interface and owned run state only with no pending input. Never replay an admitted outcome to trigger a notification. Keep private reasoning and full Task traces out of user/voice replies.

9. Time/events. Read world_cron's installed activation contract and copy its complete interface/authoring/run topology with independent state. Interval/cron schedules recur; use one-shot only if supported. A clock reaches an existing run through bindings or creates a run through its declared file-tool path. Supply the required timestamp/timezone, reminder/context and repeat semantics. Keep Home input independent of the time checkpoint. Disable a schedule by its explicit config edit; stopping a Task or call must not disable it. Other event sources use the same interface/binding rules.

10. Check results. Retain write receipts, assignment admission, later movements and required verifier/mark evidence. Distinguish authoring, emission, consumption, completion, delivery and playback when reporting the outcome; include only details useful to the task. Runtime attests policy from actual JSON. Name the failed write, role, provider, tool gate, verifier, reader or client contract when work cannot proceed.

Task names belong to the client. Supply title when run creation supports it; otherwise use the granted writer to set the task client's octopus_os.json presentation to {"name":"the requested task name","projects":[]}, preserving other fields. Names must be nonempty single-line strings of at most 80 characters. Independent worker configuration needs no saved client Agent. To reuse an Agent, inspect and select its catalog worker/template/profile; do not assign a saved identity to a new pin. Check client metadata and result evidence before reporting completion.

authoring_examples.scope: Illustrative already-authored Task and Home frontiers showing explicit assignment and result movement. Provider/door/client lives, private file-writer checkpoints, role closure, EE records and policy ids must be composed from installed descriptors before execution. These records are schema examples, not an installed Home or an executable bootstrap template.

evidence_requirements: Use admitted file/tool artifacts and any required verifier outcomes.

payload.summary: A required capability is unavailable; no effect was claimed.
remaining_gaps: Exact missing interface/tool/path and required owner action belong here.

authoring_examples.receipt_claim: task.summary.received plus artifact_exists establishes readable artifact receipt. completed/blocked/failed is producer-authored content; it never becomes a success mark merely by arriving.

ArtifactBinding.description: POLICY.md §4 — an artifact binding is the run's authored declaration of its object-level rights on a specific artifact. The `id` names the artifact; the `access` states which of read/change/create/delete the run claims on it (default: read only — a bound artifact is readable context). Formation masks this down to the worker-interface + EE verb ceiling; the interface-binding (the default flow) is a separate axis on the checkpoint.

run_record_schema.derivation: document is an exact copy of the generated source schema. The exporter includes the status and nonblank run/checkpoint trace constraints enforced by validation_source. Cross-record identity, active checkpoint bindings, policy and registry references are validated by the actual candidate validator.
